situation:
You are the customer relations manager at TIDEWATER EQUIPMENT RENTAL, a contractor rental company that merged with RIDGELINE RENTAL eleven months ago. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked you to recommend what the combined company should do about its seventy-two-hour confirmation call.

Every reservation must be confirmed by phone seventy-two hours before pickup or the machine goes back on the yard. Contractors call the rule a nuisance, and a competitor now advertises reservations with no call at all. The counter staff rely on it: the two merged branches still run separate inventory systems, and the call is the only moment anyone learns what is actually on the yard that morning.

One course is to keep the seventy-two-hour confirmation call. It protects the yard from promising machines nobody can see, but the contractors who rent by the week keep meeting a rule they dislike, and the bookings drifting to the competitor keep drifting.

The other course is to replace the call with an online reservation page, the cheapest of the two to run and the one contractors have asked for. Until the separate inventory systems are joined, though, the counter staff would be promising machines they cannot see, and a lift double-booked on a job morning costs a contractor a full day. The vice president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
